title: Three Days and One Short Bowl
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：recipe　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 recipe 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1966 the cook ① followed the recipe that no guest in the canteen would have measured, and he said the following was the whole of the day. The ② recipe, meaning the formula itself and not the bowl, ran three days and stayed unmeasured in the book; a recipe, he said, is the only thing in a canteen that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ recipe in that canteen had the same short bowl beside it, and the ④ recipe at the far table, meaning the portion they kept for the children to share and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A recipe, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the cook said the measuring is the part that fills three days.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the recipe was the whole of the matter, meaning the memory and not the formula. The ⑥ recipe, meaning the memory and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; recipe, he said, is either something you follow or the only word that means both a formula and a memory. He said the memory is the part they remember.

By 1971 the ⑦ recipe had become a line in a menu, and the menu had become an argument about the short bowl. The ⑧ recipe of the whole thing, the cook wrote in September, was one canteen and three days of measuring; recipe, he said, is either the portion at the far table or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ recipe I remember is the formula measured in the menu, which closed in 1973 and is still measured as the quietest in the canteen. A ⑩ recipe, my mother said in 1975, is the only formula that improves by being measured; every recipe, she said, is a memory that has agreed to look like a formula. She said the memory was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 食谱；配方（指食堂里每一份旁边的那一份）
B. n. 食谱；配方（指那份食谱本身，与小小的碗相对）
C. 固定搭配：follow the recipe 照着做这一份食谱
D. n. 食谱；配方（指留给孩子们分着吃的那一份）
E. n. 食谱之事（抽象总称，指一处食堂的食谱之事）
F. n. 食谱；配方（指菜单里写到、被测量的那一份）
G. n. 食谱、家传（指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 家传（抽象总称，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: followed the recipe that no guest in the canteen would have measured
The recipe, meaning the formula itself and not the bowl
the recipe at the far table
the recipe was the whole of the matter

The recipe of the whole thing
A recipe, my mother said in 1975

answers.why: follow the recipe 意为“照着做这一份食谱”，1966 年那位厨子把食堂里没有一位客人肯测量的一份食谱做了一遍。
recipe 意为“食谱；配方”，指那份食谱本身而不是小小的碗，它经过了三个日子而在簿子上没有被测量。
recipe 意为“食谱；配方”，指食堂里每一份旁边的那一份，每一份旁边都有同一只小小的碗。
recipe 意为“食谱；配方”，指最远那张桌角的留给孩子们分着吃的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
recipe 意为“食谱、家传”，指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份家传就是那件事的全部。
recipe 意为“家传”，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西而不是那份食谱，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
recipe 意为“食谱；配方”，指菜单里写到、被测量的那一份，到 1971 年这一份成了菜单里的一行。
recipe 意为“食谱之事”，厨子九月写道，整件事的食谱之事是一处食堂和三个日子的测量。
recipe 意为“食谱；配方”，我记得的是菜单里测量过的那一份，1973 年开完了，至今仍被说成食堂里最安静的一份。
recipe 为抽象总称，母亲 1975 年说，食谱是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的食谱。
